Information and Careers Guidance (IAG)
As a school, we provide Information and Career Guidance (IAG) for students in Years 7-11 through PSHCE lessons, theme days, information evenings and liaison with external providers.
This policy statement sets out the school’s arrangements for managing the access of providers to pupils at the school for the purpose of giving them information about the provider’s education or training offer. This complies with the school’s legal obligations under Section 42B of the Education Act 1997.
Students at Hounsdown School are entitled to:
Book an appointment
Find out what your options are by speaking to Mr Curtis, Hounsdown School's careers coordinator or to Hounsdown's School Careers Practitioner, Mrs Grainger (available every Thursday and Friday). The Careers Office is in West Block, ground floor.
STUDENTS: Please speak to Mr Curtis, the school's careers coordinator.
PARENTS/CARERS: Please call Mr Curtis on 023 8086 2981 or email j.curtis@hounsdown.hants.sch.uk
(All 'Career' information is reviewed on an annual basis)
Management of provider access requests
A number of events, integrated into the school careers programme, will offer providers an opportunity to come into school to speak to pupils or their parents or carers.
Please contact Mr Curtis via email at admin@hounsdown.hants.sch.uk ensuring that the email is marked for Mr Curtis's attention.
See more information on College & Apprenticeships
Careers Library
The Careers Library is housed in the main school library, where students can find up to date local Sixth Form Prospectus, information on Job seeking and Apprenticeships. We also have a full range of University Prospectus and a variety of literature on various careers.
The Careers Noticeboard is outside the library, which gives relevant information for students in Year 10 and Year 11. Tutor groups are kept up to date with resources as and when appropriate.
We also use a database called Kudos - Students can get the licence code from the noticeboard, and from all Year 11 Tutor rooms.

About our Curriculum
At Hounsdown School we are committed to provide all students with a broad, balanced, differentiated and challenging and enriching curriculum. The curriculum meets the requirements as set out in section 2 of the Education Reform Act (1988) that all students are taught Religious Education. This is undertaken at Hounsdown through the teaching of Ethics & Beliefs.
Our curriculum allows each student the opportunity to reach and achieve their potential and prepares them for the opportunities and challenges of adult life and their role and responsibilities as active citizens in modern Britain and our democratic society.

Curriculum Setting
Students are grouped for subjects in a variety of ways using setting, mixed ability teaching or broad banding as appropriate. Broad banding means that some classes will have different class labels but the same broad spread of ability. Examples of mixed ability sets include subjects such as Art, Drama, Music and PSHCE (Personal, Social, Health and Citizenship Education).
When creating a group setting system we use benchmarking data (KS2 & KS3 results), CATS, Reading Ages and Spelling Ages alongside on-going teacher assessment. Staff in school make the final decision about setting. Setting, where it occurs, is reviewed departmentally at the end of every term and any individual changes to setting will be notified to parents and carers through a formal letter home.
Subjects are grouped together in to blocks to make the timetable work. English and Maths are never in the same block, which means students may be in different sets for English and Maths, as appropriate for the ability.
Setting starts with a broad range of abilities in each set early in Year 7 and is refined over time as teachers get a better understanding of the student’s work. Students are quite likely to change sets over their school career, such that they are best placed in each set to help them make good progress.

Special Educational Needs & Disabilities
At Hounsdown School we welcome everybody into our community. The school’s motto is “Be the best that you can be” which drives our curriculum design and approach to learning.
Every student has the opportunity to follow National Curriculum subjects as well as following an appropriate GCSE curriculum pathway. Our options programme allows for personalisation, with additional time in the core subjects should it be needed.
We are committed to narrowing the attainment gap between SEND and non-SEND students. This may include after school interventions, short-term intervention learning or other learning interventions developed on an individual needs basis.
We have good attendance at Hounsdown School as students want to come to school to experience our high quality learning environment.
If your child has a special educational need or disability and you would like to know more about what we offer at Hounsdown School after reading these pages contact us on 02380862981 or e-mail us at admin@hounsdown.hants.sch.uk, asking for the SENCO to contact you.

Absence & Attendance
If your child is going to be absent from school including arriving late, please let the school know by 08:30. Please let us know by 08:30 every day they are off.
On the day of absence, you can notify us using the Arbor Parent Portal or Arbor App. Alternatively, you can call 02380 862981 (option 1) leaving a message with the following information...
1. The student's name2. Tutor Group3. Nature of illness / appointment4. Expected return date / time
If we are not contacted by 08:30, we will contact parents / carers via text. Please ensure that you respond.
Our Attendance Policy can be found under the 'General Policies' section on our 'School Policies' webpage.
School Attendance Lead / Champion:
Miss Ellard, Assistant Headteacher (Strategic oversight on Attendance Management)
We recognise that good attendance is important in helping young people to achieve socially, academically and to develop important skills beyond their time with us.
Students should be in school every day, and their attendance will ideally be 100%, however, we recognise that at times there maybe illness / medical appointments. All students should strive for 96%+ attendance over an academic year. Where possible, students’ medical appointments should be made outside of school hours. Absence impacts learning time and progress.
At times we know that some students may experience difficulties coming into school and we would ask that you contact your child’s tutor with any concerns in the first instance.
As a school, we will celebrate good attendance.
More information

Students are registered at the start of every lesson
Statutory registration is 8:30-9am every day (am session) and Period 4 at 12:10pm (pm session). Registers are taken during tutor / assembly time. Any student arriving after the register closes will be marked late (L).
Any student arriving after 9am will be marked present when they sign in at Student Services and will receive a U code. This means they are counted as absent for the am session of the day.
Leaving School Premises
Students must have a note in their log book, signed by their parent/carer or by adding a notification to Class Charts, for any period they will be leaving the school premises during school hours.
Before leaving the school premises, the student must visit Student Services to sign out with the note.
Where possible, medical appointments should be made outside of the school day.
Late Arrivals
Any student arriving after tutor time finishes, must report to Student Services to sign in.
Arrival after 9am will be marked as 'U' code and will not be counted as an authorised attendance. Please ensure Student Services are notified for planned late arrivals by either adding a note to Class Charts or by a written / signed note in the student's logbook.
Student Services and Medical Room Provision
Students must have a note in their log book, signed by their parent/carer or by adding a notification to Class Charts if they have an appointment out of school during the school day, e.g. dental / hospital appointment / college interview. Students must inform their Tutor / the teacher taking the lesson impacted, and sign out in the Student Services Office.
Students must sign back in again upon their return to school.
Leave of Absence from School Request (LOAF)
Please ensure that any evidence is attached to the LOAF form to support your request. The completed form must be submitted 7 days prior to the event.
The LOAF form should also be completed, if the request is for a full day's medical appointment. If the absence is for exceptional circumstances please add as much detail as possible.
Absence for Family Holidays or other reasons
Regular attendance by all students is both a legal requirement and essential for consistent progress and achievement for a student to reach their full educational potential.
Parents/carers and teachers share the responsibility for supporting and promoting excellent school attendance and punctuality. It is our shared duty to consistently strive to achieve a goal of 100% attendance for all students.
Despite a recent national legal challenge, the law states that Headteachers cannot grant leave of absence during term time, unless there are exceptional circumstances (rare, significant and unavoidable events). It is at the discretion of the Headteacher if leave is authorised. Please be aware, such absence can lead to the issue of Fixed Penalty Notices (fines) for non-attendance or persistent unauthorised attendance.
Following a review of the law by the Supreme Court the school will follow the latest Hampshire County Council guidance on issuing Fixed Penalty Notices.
All requests for student's 'leave of absence' must be made by completing the following form and emailing it to admin@hounsdown.hants.sch.uk.

Admissions
The Trustees of Hounsdown School are the admission authority for the school. They have chosen to adopt Hampshire County council's admission policy which was in place prior to the school gaining academy status on 01 August 2011. Hounsdown School works closely with the Local Authority to ensure that the school's admission arrangements are complied with.
The current published admission number (PAN) for Hounsdown School is 261.
Hounsdown Catchment Area
Click on the following sections to see more information about...
Moving from Year 6 to Year 7
Most of our students join us at the beginning of Year 7 (aged 11), primarily from our three local linked primary schools, Foxhills, Abbotswood and Bartley.
Transition from primary to secondary school is an exciting time for all, although we recognise that some may feel anxiety about the change. We work closely with students and parents to ensure that everyone settles quickly into school life here at Hounsdown.
For more information, see our dedicated Year 6 to Year 7 page.
Frequently asked Questions
If you have any specific questions about the transition from Year 6 to Year 7, then please email us at Transition@hounsdown.hants.sch.uk.
Our Admissions Process
Applications for admission to Year 7 are conducted by the Local Authority during the first half of the autumn term when children are in Year 6.
Parents of children in Year 6 will receive information about the application process from their child’s current primary school.
Parents and carers are informed of places allocated by the Local Authority shortly after their list is published.
Applying for a place 'in-year'
Applications for admission to any year group, can be considered at any time. To apply for an 'in-year' place at Hounsdown School, please complete the Hounsdown School Application Form in accordance with the guidance notes at the end of the application form.
You will receive a reply in writing from the school, normally within 10 school days.
Alternatively, you can complete the in-year application form online at: www.hants.gov.uk/admissions

Our Prospectus
I hope that our prospectus below reflects the enormous pride that we have in our school. Hounsdown is a highly successful and popular school with a strong emphasis on the traditional values of hard work, honesty, responsibility and respect for others.
Our school has high expectations of students, staff, parents and trustees alike and we work in close partnership in order to ensure that everyone strives to give of their best. We especially value our collaboration with parents; working together to ensure every young person in our care is challenged and reaches their full potential.

School Uniform
Hounsdown is a school proud of its ethos, values and standards. We want students in their uniform to reflect that pride, knowing they belong to such a strong community.
In order to maintain good standards of dress and personal appearance, which are sensible and appropriate for students, please review our School Uniform Policy (under 'General Policies' section). This avoids inequalities of dress and extremes of fashion which are often quite unsuitable for work at school.
Any student wearing incorrect uniform will be told to correct it and a mark will be placed on their uniform tracker. Each time a row on the tracker is completed, a sanction will be put in place by the tutor. Should uniform breaches happen on a regular basis, parents will be asked to attend a meeting with the tutor to discuss a way forward. The Behaviour Policy will be applied for any refusal to follow a reasonable instruction to amend uniform during the school day.
If you are unsure about any aspect of our school uniform, please contact the school for clarification. We are happy to provide advice and guidance on what is acceptable for school before any purchases are made.
Please remember that we also hold good quality ‘pre-loved’ uniform that can be purchased by emailing uniform@hounsdown.hants.sch.uk.
There is also school uniform grant which can be applied for by parent/carers via the form on the website.
Uniform should be worn as follows:
Application for School Uniform Grant
Shirt
White shirt that must have a top button that fastens. The shirt can be short or long sleeved.
School ties
To be worn by all boys in Year's 8 to 11 and all students in Year 7.
Jumper
Black V neck jumper with the school logo (available from Skoolkit and Koolskools).
Blazer
Plain black blazer with the school logo (available from Skoolkit).
Please note: Students must have their jumper or blazer with them at all times. Students are permitted to wear their coats over their school jumper or blazer, not instead of. Coats must be removed in all lessons. Students may choose to wear both a blazer and jumper, should they wish to.Hooded Jumpers (Hoodies). Hooded zip up tracksuit tops or cardigans are not permitted. Any other type of jumper is not permitted. These will be confiscated and available for collection at the end of the school day.
Skirt
Tartan skirt in Hounsdown colours available from Skoolkit. Skirts should not be rolled up and should be worn between mid-thigh and the knee.
Trousers
Full length plain black trousers that are not rolled up. The trousers must be identifiable as trousers, with a fastening at the waistband. Combat / Leggings /Jeggings /Jeans / Tracksuit bottom / sportswear must not be worn in any circumstance as uniform. Skin-tight material is not permitted.
Tailored shorts
Plain black tailored shorts – mid thigh to knee. The tailored shorts must be identifiable as shorts with a fastening at the waistband. Combat / Leggings / Jeggings / Jeans / Tracksuit bottom / sportswear must not be worn in any circumstances as uniform. Skin tight material is not permitted.
Shoes
Plain black shoes, safe and suitable, completely black including branding, logos, laces, and soles with enclosed toes. No boots or heels.
Socks/tights
Socks can be plain, white, grey or black – ankle length. Tights must be plain black, no holes or fashion style.
Coats/outer garments
Coats must not be worn instead of a jumper or blazer. Coats should be suitable for all weather conditions and be identifiable as a coat. Fleece hooded tops/tracksuit tops/ zip up hoodies/jackets are not coats suitable for school. Coats which help with visibility in the dark would be advisable when travelling to school.
Nails
Nails must be a safe length to be able to access all curriculum lessons and activities. They should be natural in colour. No false nails or extensions.
Make-up
Discreet, subtle make-up may be worn in Years 9-11.
Jewellery
We do not recommend that any items of jewellery are worn in school.
Should students choose to wear jewellery, it must be safe, sensible, and able to be removed for practical lessons/activities/health and safety reasons. Should students choose to wear jewellery then the following is allowed: small stud piercings only (no hoops, no drop earrings, no stretchers, no bars, no chains and not dangling).
For health and safety reasons the taping of any jewellery is not permitted in PE/Dance lessons. It must be removed.
Any items of jewellery brought into school are the sole responsibility of the student.
Hair style
Students’ hairstyles should be safe, sensible and tied back for all practical lessons/activities/health and safety reasons. Students with long hair should ensure that they have hair bands with them.
PE kit
Compulsory Items
Gum shields (for rugby).
Shin pads (for football).
Waterproof/plastic bag for soiled items.
Amendments to school uniform policy
Hounsdown School has the right to require any student to remove a garment of uniform/jewellery (or item being worn to school) which we deem unsafe and/or not upholding the ethos of the school and/or considered to be associated with a gang/crime/drugs paraphernalia.

Cycling Guidelines
Cyclists' Code
When meeting traffic, keep to the left.
When overtaking, always pass on the right.
Be courteous to other road users.
Always ride in single file.
Never carry anyone on your cycle.
Never carry items hanging from your handlebars.
Cycling Rules
Cyclists are forbidden to cross the A35, other than by using the designated traffic lighted crossing points or the underpass near Players Crescent. In both cases, cyclists should give priority to pedestrians and be careful passing them.
It is illegal to cycle on the pedestrian pathways. The Police, however, agree that it is dangerous to cycle to/from school on certain roads in our catchment area. Unofficially, they agree not to prevent pupils from using the path for cycling, providing that pupils look out for the pedestrians using the path and pass then very slowly, dismounting if necessary.
